activity.message:
ci: drop the unused Setup Pages step

actions/configure-pages reads the Pages site's base URL and configures static
site generators such as Next.js and Nuxt. This site is plain HTML and uses
none of its outputs. The step also reads the Pages API, which the build job
does not have permission for now that its permissions are limited to what it
needs, so it could only add a failure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(readme): describe the data flow, checks, AI assistance and the license

The README did not say what the workflow publishes, why the daily data commit
is made by the Actions bot, or how to recover when GitHub disables the
scheduled workflow after 60 idle days. Document those, the checks, a plain
statement that the dashboard was first generated with Gemini and has been
reworked with Claude Code, and the license.

Use the workspace branch prefixes (feat/, fix/, refactor/) instead of
feature/, bugfix/ and chore/, so the README and the workspace rules agree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: add editor settings and agent instruction files

Add .editorconfig and .gitattributes from the workspace template, and an
AGENTS.md that records the stack, the file-by-file architecture, the commands
and the constraints a new session needs. The main one: the daily data commit
must stay under the Actions bot identity, or it fills the owner's
contribution graph again. CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md only import AGENTS.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(data): leave bot commits out of Recent Activity

The daily data commit made by GitHub Actions, and commits by agents such as
Jules, are not the owner's activity, but they filled the Recent Activity
list: 10 of its 15 entries were data updates. Ask the API for each commit's
author name and skip names that end in "[bot]".

The script ran on import, which made the filter impossible to test. Read the
token inside the fetch function and run it only when the file is executed
directly. Add unit tests for the filter with `node --test` (no dependency)
and run them in the workflow before fetching.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: bound the data fetch and move the schedule off the hour

- A hung request to the GitHub API would have held the job until the default
  six-hour limit. Abort the fetch after 30 seconds and give both jobs a
  10-minute timeout.
- GitHub documents that scheduled runs are delayed most at the start of each
  hour. The recent runs started about four hours after the 00:00 schedule.
  Run at 03:17 UTC instead.
- Run `npm run check` before fetching so a syntax error fails the build early.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: update workflow actions to current major versions and Node 24

The Actions runner already forced these v4-era actions onto Node 24 and
reported "Node.js 20 is deprecated" on every run. Move to the current majors
(checkout v7, setup-node v7, configure-pages v6, upload-pages-artifact v5,
deploy-pages v5) and run the fetch script on Node 24 as well.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: publish only site files and commit refreshed data as the Actions bot

The workflow uploaded the whole repository (`path: '.'`) to GitHub Pages, so
node_modules/, scripts/, package files and the README were publicly served.
`scripts/build-site.js` now copies an allow-list (index.html, css/, js/,
data/data.json) into _site/ and only that folder is deployed.

The daily data commit stays, but it must not look like the owner's work. A
commit counts toward a profile's contribution graph only when its author email
is linked to that account. 9d08bc1 switched the commit identity from the
Actions bot to the owner; in the last year those 198 commits were 22.6% of the
875 contributions, and on 147 of the 216 active days the data commit was the
only contribution. Commit as github-actions[bot] again, and only on main so a
manual run from another branch cannot push.

Also split the workflow into build and deploy jobs: only the build job gets
`contents: write`, only the deploy job gets `pages: write` and `id-token:
write`, and deployments are queued instead of running in parallel.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: add the MIT license and a third-party notice

The repository is public but had no license, which leaves all rights reserved.
Add the MIT license with the author as copyright holder, and record the one
development dependency and the actions the workflow uses, with licenses taken
from the lockfile and from GitHub.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore(package): correct package metadata and replace the placeholder test

- `main` pointed at an index.js that does not exist.
- `npm test` ran `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`, so it could
  only fail. Replace it with `npm run check`, a syntax check of every script.
- The license was ISC; the workspace rule for this account is MIT.
- Mark the package private so it cannot be published by accident, name the
  author, and declare the Node version the scripts need (fs.cp is stable from
  Node 22).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(ui): remove a no-op sidebar rule and a stale comment

`.sidebar { position: static }` in the narrow-screen block did nothing: no rule
makes the sidebar sticky or fixed, so it was always static. It is a leftover
from an earlier layout. The insights grid comment also described a 2x4 layout
that has not existed for a while.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #5 from kosuke-satake/feat/message-protocol

Specify the brain-body message format and implement it on the body

Merge pull request #4 from kosuke-satake/docs/member-branches

Document personal branches for hardware members

Point the READMEs and guides to the message protocol

Stage 1 now has a defined message format, so the status lines move on
to choosing the parts, and the software guide names protocol.md as the
reference every implementation follows.

Add a line reader for serial input

Serial delivers bytes, not lines. The reader is fed whatever has
arrived and reports each complete line, so the main loop never waits.
A line that is too long or contains a NUL is dropped whole rather than
cut, so a truncated command can never be parsed as a valid one.

Parse velocity commands and format odometry on the body

Implements docs/protocol.md for the body side. The number check is
stricter than strtof, which would also accept exponents, hexadecimal,
nan and inf. A rejected line leaves the last command untouched, and an
invalid state produces no line rather than being reported as OK.
